money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Leone (SLL). Euros and US dollars are the easiest foreign currencies to exchange. Only exchange money at banks and official exchange bureaus. The economy is cash-based. There are strict rules limiting the amount of foreign cash that can be brought into the country. Consult with the nearest embassy or consulate of Sierra Leone for the latest details. Credit cards and traveller's cheques aren't widely accepted. There aren't many ATMs in Freetown. Contact your bank to check if your cards will work in Sierra Leone.

laws.rule: Engaging in same-sex activity is illegal and could lead to prison sentences, including life imprisonment. LGBTQIA+ relationships and identities are widely regarded as unacceptable. There are reports of discrimination and violence against LGBTQIA+ people in Sierra Leone. There is no recognition of same-sex relationships.
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ information

laws.rule: Don't use, carry or traffic illegal drugs. Penalties for drug offences are severe and include mandatory terms. Prison conditions in Sierra Leone are hard.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: You can drive for one month with a valid Australian driver's licence (digital driver’s licences may not be accepted) an International Driving Permit (IDP) After that, you'll need a local licence. You must get your IDP before you leave Australia.
laws.heading: Driving permit

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Tolerant, multi-religious culture; respect local customs. Carry ID (a copy of the passport photo page and visa is usually accepted). Do not photograph military sites, government buildings, prisons or courthouses; people have been arrested. Same-sex relations between men are illegal. Diamond smuggling carries heavy penalties.
culture-and-protocol.note: From UK Government (FCDO) travel advice, written for British travellers but the laws apply to all visitors. Confirm locally.

events.what: Ramadan, the Muslim month of fasting, expected about 8 February to 8 or 9 March 2027 (set by moon sighting)
events.effect: Many Muslims fast from dawn to sunset. Some cafés and restaurants close by day and business hours shorten; eating, drinking or smoking in public in daylight can cause offence. Evenings are busy after the fast is broken.
Public holiday: government offices, banks and many businesses close.
